newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-BRONSON LOSS A SALUTARY REMINDER TO BATTEN.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BRONSON LOSS A SALUTARY REMINDER TO BATTEN.

text.p: American favourite Bryan Bronson's defeat in the world men's 400 metres hurdles final has served as a salutary reminder to team mate Kim Batten.
"You cannot race in the 400 metres hurdles against your opponent," said the defending women's champion and world record holder on Tuesday.
Bronson, who had the three fastest times in the world this season before the championships, never developed a proper rhythm in Monday's final and ended with the bronze.
"It will be important that I run my own race," Batten said of the probable rematch with Olympic champion Deon Hemmings on Friday. "I cannot get caught up in racing.
"Stride pattern is going to determine this race and as long as I stay with my stride pattern I don't think I'm going to have a problem."
Both Batten and Hemmings have predicted the world record of 52.61 set at the 1995 Gothenburg world championships will fall on Friday.
Batten clocked 52.97 at the U.S. championships and Hemmings returned 53.18 in Oslo last month.
